description: The provided image displays three side-by-side bar charts labeled (a) WikiText, (b), and (c) C4, each comparing the perplexity of two methods—"Uniform" (blue bars) and "Ours" (orange bars)—across varying numbers of quantization bits. In each chart, the horizontal axis represents "Quantization Bits," with tick marks at 3, 4, 8, and 16, while the vertical axis represents "Perplexity," scaled linearly. Chart (a) shows perplexity values ranging from 0 to 30, with the "Uniform" method achieving a perplexity of approximately 29.5 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 26.5 at 4 bits, then stabilizing near 26 at 8 and 16 bits, while "Ours" remains consistently lower, around 21.5 to 22. Chart (b) uses a different scale for perplexity, ranging from 0 to 400, where "Uniform" starts at approximately 400 at 3 bits and decreases to around 310 at 4 bits, then stabilizes near 300 at 8 and 16 bits, while "Ours" remains significantly lower, around 250 to 180. Chart (c) uses a vertical axis scaled from 0 to 30, where "Uniform" starts at approximately 29.5 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 25 at 4 bits, then stabilizing near 25 at 8 and 16 bits, while "Ours" remains consistently lower, around 21 to 18. In all three charts, the bars are grouped by quantization bit value, with the "Uniform" method consistently represented by blue bars and "Ours" by orange bars, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and height.
